questions.prompt: What is the safest way to use a type or build feature?
options: Use any whenever the types become difficult.
Treat type-level examples as proof of runtime correctness.
Choose the feature that expresses the contract, check compiler diagnostics, and verify the configured tool/runtime behavior.
Assume compiler configuration has identical behavior in every version.
questions.answer_key: Choose the feature that expresses the contract, check compiler diagnostics, and verify the configured tool/runtime behavior.
questions.explanation: Type and build features must be evaluated in the actual configured project.

questions.prompt: Which statement is correct about “Environment-Specific Configurations”?
options: The learner should publish hidden solutions so the exercise can grade itself.
The concept should be demonstrated with development and production settings and checked against its intended contract.
The safest approach is to skip diagnostics and trust the first output.
A type assertion automatically validates every value at runtime.
questions.answer_key: The concept should be demonstrated with development and production settings and checked against its intended contract.
questions.explanation: The supplied syllabus explicitly includes “Development and production settings”; connect it to a concrete example and verify the behavior relevant to this lesson.

questions.prompt: What is a good verification step after practicing “Environment-Specific Configurations”?
options: Check shared configuration, include a meaningful failure case where appropriate, and document any runtime or version assumptions.
Assume browser, node.js, and test environments is unnecessary because the code has type annotations.
Ignore compiler or test failures if the interface looks correct.
Treat passing a static token check as proof that the program executed correctly.
questions.answer_key: Check shared configuration, include a meaningful failure case where appropriate, and document any runtime or version assumptions.
questions.explanation: The syllabus includes “Shared configuration”. Verification should match the concept: type-level checks, runtime tests, configuration checks or human review as appropriate.
